title: Staged regional snapshot snapback runbook and adaptive load-shedding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Runbook and validation plan for an active-passive regional evacuation that uses progressive region promotion, snapshot-based KV snapback ordering, and adaptive load-shedding driven by circuit-breaker telemetry. Goal: verify end-to-end restore correctness, meet SLO degradation budgets during a scheduled drill, and validate automated rollback paths. This ticket produces the executable playbook, verification harness, dashboards, and post-drill verification checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Automated drill completes with documented timings for snapshot export, import, and reconciled KV state
SLOs observed: p95 latency < 350ms for 95% of requests through the drill window or documented trade-offs and compensating controls
Circuit-breaker thresholds trigger expected shedding behaviors and revert cleanly when load reduces
No missing keys after two-phase KV snapback verification (compare checksums + hash sampling)
Rollback path (reconnect active region) validated in <= 15 minutes in a dry run
Runbook reviewed and approved by Oncall, Reliability, and Security (review comments addressed)
steps: Pre-drill: validate snapshots retained for last 24h in s3://redwood-drsnapshots/region-A/ with successful checksum verification
Pre-drill: run smoke load against passive region with 10% of baseline traffic and confirm routing policy can accept canary tags
Step 1: freeze writes to active region via staged toggles (API toggle + ingress weight 0 -> maintenance header) and confirm 200ms drain window
Step 2: export KV snapshot at consistent point (coordinated flush + raft snapshot) and copy to passive region; verify checksums
Step 3: promote passive region to active via control-plane API with sequenced DNS TTL reduction and BGP announcement script
Step 4: import KV snapshot into promoted region using ordered restore (meta -> keys -> kv-values) and apply background sync for write-ahead entries
Step 5: enable adaptive load-shedding policy: per-route shedding percentages from 5% -> 50% keyed by observed CPU token rate and queue depth thresholds
Step 6: set circuit-breaker thresholds: p50 latency plateau 300ms => increase shedding; queue_length > 200 => reject + 429 with Retry-After header
Step 7: ramp traffic in 3 waves (1%, 10%, 100%) with automated monitoring gates and abort criteria for error spikes
Step 8: reconciliation: run checksum sampling across hot KV prefixes and run consistency jobs; escalate if >0.1% mismatch
Step 9: verification: run representative end-to-end eval prompt set (50 prompts) and compare embeddings + tokens for semantic drift
Step 10: rollback: if abort criteria met, demote new region and reattach routing to original active region using BGP teardown and control-plane rollback scripts
smoke_tests: Healthcheck endpoint /_health returns ok from promoted region
Tokenstore basic read/write test across 100 keys within <50ms median
Embedding pipeline end-to-end inference for a 128-token prompt under 400ms median
metrics_to_monitor: rate of rejections from circuit breakers
KV restore throughput (keys/sec) and snapshot import duration
cache hit ratio for prefix/KV cache
CPU/GPU utilization and queue depth on serving nodes
